## TL;DR

I walked the Hub server picker, the add-server form, the rename sheet and the tailnet discovery screen headlessly in Chromium at 375, 768 and 1280 widths. Layout held in every state I measured: no document overflow, no element past the viewport edge, no console errors, and every Tab-focused control showed a focus cue. The one real defect was keyboard-related. The rename sheet is a modal dialog, but opening it from the keyboard left focus on the row behind the scrim, and Escape did nothing. I fixed that in `BottomSheet` and added a jsdom regression test. I also extended the committed sweep (`mobile/scripts/hub-picker-qa.ts`) to six viewports, including 375 and 1280. It passes 510 of 510 checks. The limits are stated below: Chromium only, mocked network, and no device pass.

## Work and rationale

The task says "projects switcher". In the Hub, each saved server is a RepoOS project, so the switcher is the server picker in `mobile/`. The web TopBar has a project chip, but it opens a colour picker, not a switcher, so I kept the scope to `mobile/`.

I started with the existing #1242 sweep as a baseline. It passed 340 of 340 checks, but it only covers the add-server form, at 360, 412, 768 and 1024. It never touches the picker list, switching, discovery, or 375 and 1280. So I wrote one-off Playwright walks, kept out of the repo, that visit each fixture state (many, one, empty, unreachable, add, discover) at all three widths. They measure document overflow, out-of-bounds elements, console errors and a Tab-driven focus-cue check. Those walks found nothing, and I took screenshots to confirm the metrics. The picker, sheet and forms are capped at 560px, so the 1280 view shows a centred column. I checked the CSS and treated that as deliberate, not as a layout bug.

The rename sheet walk is where the defect was. Opening it with Enter left `document.activeElement` on "Edit dev", outside the dialog, and Escape did not close it. `BottomSheet.vue` now moves focus to the panel on open. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside the panel, and the scrim stays out of the tab order. Escape emits `close`, and closing returns focus to the control that opened the sheet. The panel gets `outline: none` because it is a container, not a control. Focus goes to the panel rather than the name input, because focusing a text field on a phone raises the on-screen keyboard as soon as the sheet opens.

The branch already carried an earlier focus-ring fix on `.field input:focus` (a 1px `box-shadow` ring), pinned by `mobile-hub-picker-layout.test.ts`. I kept it as is.

The committed sweep now runs six viewports: 360, 375, 412, 768×1024, 1024×768 and 1280×800. Its output is 510/510. I added a #1271 section to `docs/qa/2026-11-hub-picker-qa.md` that records the widths, the sheet fix and what was not covered.

## Approaches tried

- **Scratch walks, then a committed regression test.** The walks checked the outcome, but nothing in the repo would catch a future regression in focus handling. So the sheet behaviour has a table-driven jsdom test (`src/ui-app/tests/mobile-bottom-sheet-focus.test.ts`). It covers focus on open, the three wrap cases, Escape, and focus return. The keyboard probe was also rerun in Chromium at 375, 768 and 1280, and passed at all three.
- **Focusing the name input on open.** Rejected, as above. The focus-the-panel approach is safer on touch devices.
- **Widening the picker to full width at 1280.** Not done. The 560px cap is shared by the picker, the sheet and the forms. Changing it is a design decision, not a QA fix.
- **Reading the reachability "Checking…" label.** The `many` fixture sets every server to "Reachable" without a network call, so I could not drive the checking state through fixtures. I did not fake it. It is listed as not covered.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Test runner config.** A bare `bunx vitest run <file>` fails on any test that imports a `.vue` file, because the root config has no Vue plugin. The project config works: `bunx vitest run --config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts <file>`. The existing add-server test fails the same way under the bare command, so this is a runner-invocation note, not a code problem.
- **Formatter.** The first scoped check failed `check-fmt` on my new test file. `bun run fmt` reflowed one long string literal and nothing else.
- **Earlier handoff failure.** The last handoff failed with "Engineering report draft is missing: .repoos/engineering-report-drafts/1271.md", though that file existed in the worktree. The path is gitignored under `.repoos/*`, so the cause could be that the server reads it from somewhere other than this worktree. I did not confirm the cause. This draft is rewritten in the same path, and I will report whether the next handoff accepts it.

## Key learnings

- A visual sweep can pass every metric and still miss modal keyboard behaviour. Overflow and cue checks don't tell you where focus went. For any dialog, check focus-in, Tab containment, Escape, and focus return explicitly.
- Fixtures can hide states. A fixture that pins reachability to "Reachable" means the "Checking…" label is never on screen in a fixture walk, so it needs a network-level probe or a dedicated fixture.
- The same gap exists elsewhere, and I did not widen the fix to it. The update dialog in `mobile/src/App.vue` is a dev-only `role="dialog"` with no focus or Escape handling. It is outside the picker flow, so it is a follow-up. `AddServerView` also has an unused edit mode (the "Done" label is never shown, since App only mounts it with `mode="add"`). I left it alone because it is dead code, not a user-facing defect.

## Not covered

No real device, Android WebView or iOS WKWebView was used, and Chromium differs from both. The network is mocked, so "unreachable" and "slow" describe how the app handles mocked replies, not a real server. Touch targets, the on-screen keyboard and the Android back gesture were not exercised. A human needs a device pass before this is called verified on device.
